newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM's party says open to price control talks.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM's party says open to price control talks.

text.p: Deputies from the ruling Czech centre-right Civic Democratic Party (ODS) said on Wednesday they were ready to negotiate with their coalition partners who are demanding fast decisions on price deregulation and taxes.

But the same deputies comprising ODS's parliamentary caucus said they considered "irresponsible" the pro-business Civic Democratic Alliance's (ODA) conditioning of support for the 1997 state budget vote on setting a timetable for energy and housing rent liberalisation and tax cuts.

"(As to) the suggestions brought up by the ODA...the ODS (parliamentary) club considers them to be important and is ready to negotiate about them," dupties of the ODS, led by Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, said in a joint statement.
The ODA said it would support the 1997 draft budget in its final readings later this month only if a timetable for liberalising these controlled prices and tax cuts were taken.

Leaders of the coalition, which includes the centrist Christian-Democratic Union (KDU-CSL), met late Tuesday night to discuss their approach to the upcoming 1997 budget debate but did not consider ODA's demands, the local daily Hodspodarske Noviny said on Wednesday.
But the paper said they agreed that the 1997 balanced state budget draft should not be amended in any way when debated in the parliament before a final vote later this month.
The coalition lost its majority in the Chamber of Deputies in the general election last spring, winning 99 of 200 seats, making every vote for final budget approval crucial.
ODA has 13 votes in parliament and four cabinet seats.
The budget draft passed its first reading thanks to four opposition Social Democrats who crossed party ranks.
The final two readings of the budget are expected to go to parliament in the session which begins on December 10.
